content.text: Since radioactivity originates in the nucleus (not the orbital electrons), it's completely independent of chemical bonding or environmental conditions.

When an unstable nucleus decays, it forms a new nuclide called a
, which may itself be stable or may require a whole chain of further transformations before reaching a stable end product.
Unstable nuclei return toward stability through one of several decay modes:
A neutron converts to a proton, emitting an electron and antineutrino
A proton converts to a neutron, emitting a positron and neutrino
An atomic electron is captured, converting a proton to a neutron
The nucleus emits a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons)
Gamma emission and internal conversion also occur, typically after another decay mode leaves the daughter nucleus in an excited state that then releases energy as a gamma photon.
